security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, PyTorch eval mode, normal imports, HDF5 storage, memory mapping, and dataset globbing. The confirmed issue is optional SegmentMIFRemote documentation that points pathology image processing to DeepCell remote APIs, which can expose sensitive clinical image data if used without consent or de-identification. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.issue: Remote inference can send pathology image data to DeepCell APIs.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit warnings requiring de-identification, consent, and institutional approval before SegmentMIFRemote use; prefer local SegmentMIF by default.

remediation.issue: The SLURM batch example passes slide paths through shell variables.
remediation.suggestion: Quote $SLIDE_PATH in the generated script and document that slide lists should come from trusted project directories.

remediation.issue: Filesystem examples create helper files and feature arrays in local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to run examples inside a project workspace and choose output paths intentionally to avoid overwriting existing files.

semantic_findings.description: The documentation recommends SegmentMIFRemote with DeepCell API URLs for remote segmentation, but does not warn users about sending pathology image channels to an external service. Clinical image data may require consent, de-identification, and institutional approval before external processing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly configure remote DeepCell API inference for image segmentation. The risk depends on the user data, but pathology images are commonly sensitive clinical data.

content.value_statement: Whole-slide pathology workflows require specialized image loading, preprocessing, graph analysis, and model guidance. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use PathML for reproducible computational pathology tasks.
actual_capabilities: Guides loading whole-slide images from formats such as SVS, NDPI, DICOM, OME-TIFF, CODEX, and Vectra.
Explains PathML preprocessing pipelines for tissue detection, stain normalization, artifact labeling, and nucleus detection.
Describes spatial graph construction from cell coordinates, morphology, intensity features, and tissue context.
Provides workflows for HoVer-Net, HACTNet, PyTorch training, evaluation metrics, and ONNX inference.
Covers multiparametric imaging workflows for CODEX, Vectra, Mesmer segmentation, marker quantification, and AnnData export.
Documents HDF5 storage, tile management, batch processing, feature storage, and memory-mapped arrays.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not include a verified PathML runtime or bundled datasets.
It does not replace clinical review, diagnostic validation, or regulated medical device approval.
Large slide processing still depends on local storage, memory, GPU availability, and installed PathML dependencies.
Remote DeepCell examples may send image data to an external service and require privacy review before use.

use_cases.title: Prepare Histology Slides
use_cases.description: Plan loading, tiling, tissue detection, and stain normalization for H&E whole-slide image analysis.

use_cases.title: Build Spatial Feature Workflows
use_cases.description: Create cell graphs, extract morphology and intensity features, and prepare graph data for downstream modeling.

use_cases.title: Manage Large Pathology Datasets
use_cases.description: Organize tiles, masks, features, and metadata with HDF5 storage and batch processing patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Slide Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new WSI task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a PathML workflow for loading SVS slides, generating tiles, detecting tissue, and saving processed outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Preprocessing Steps
prompt_templates.scenario: Select transforms for H&E image quality and normalization.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a PathML preprocessing pipeline for H&E slides with tissue detection, stain normalization, artifact checks, and nucleus detection.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multiplex Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Analyze CODEX or multiplex immunofluorescence data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PathML workflow for CODEX data that segments cells, quantifies markers, and exports results for single-cell analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Training Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced model training and evaluation planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PathML model training plan for HoVer-Net, including data loading, validation metrics, inference, and storage of extracted features.

output_examples.input: I need to process 200 H&E whole-slide images for tissue and nucleus analysis.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow covering slide loading, tiling level choice, tissue masking, stain normalization, nucleus detection, HDF5 storage, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: I have CODEX images and need marker expression by cell.
output_examples.output: A multiparametric analysis plan that collapses runs, segments cells, quantifies markers, stores spatial coordinates, and exports AnnData.

output_examples.input: My pathology feature extraction pipeline is too slow.
output_examples.output: A performance review with tile-size guidance, pyramid level selection, Dask batch processing, feature caching, and memory-mapped storage options.

best_practices: Validate preprocessing on representative sample slides before scaling to a full cohort.
Keep clinical image data de-identified and avoid remote APIs unless approval is documented.
Store intermediate tiles, masks, metadata, and features in reproducible project directories.
anti_patterns: Do not treat model outputs as clinical diagnoses without validated medical review.
Do not send protected image data to remote inference services without privacy approval.
Do not process full-resolution slides unnecessarily when lower pyramid levels meet the task requirements.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users apply PathML concepts to computational pathology workflows involving whole-slide images and multiplex imaging data.

faq.question: Does it install PathML automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents installation and workflow patterns, but users must manage their own Python environment and dependencies.

faq.question: Can it analyze clinical cases by itself?
faq.answer: No. It supports research workflow planning and code guidance, not autonomous diagnosis or clinical decision-making.

faq.question: Which image types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers whole-slide and microscopy formats such as SVS, NDPI, DICOM, OME-TIFF, CODEX, Vectra, and related formats.

faq.question: Does it support machine learning workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for PyTorch training, HoVer-Net, HACTNet, evaluation metrics, inference, and feature extraction.

faq.question: What security caution matters most?
faq.answer: Remote DeepCell examples may send image data outside the local environment, so users should review privacy and consent requirements first.
